marks.gloss_en: כתיב הכא 'לפני בת בליעל' וכתיב התם 'יצאו אנשים בני בליעל' (Deut 13:14, the idolatrous city) -- מה להלן עבודה זרה אף כאן עבודה זרה: the drunk who prays is as if he worships idols
from here, a drunk who prays is as if he worships idols
מכאן -- Hannah told Eli she had not drunk
from here, one suspected of something that is not in him must inform [the suspecter]
מכאן -- Eli answered her 'go in peace'
שנאמר ואלהי ישראל יתן את שלתך -- Eli blessed her
from here, one who suspects his fellow of something that is not in him must appease him
'no, my lord': she said to him, you are not a master in this matter, nor does the holy spirit rest upon you, that you suspect me of this

thus she said to him: are you not a master? is the Shekhina and holy spirit not with you, that you judged me guilty and did not judge me innocent? did you not know that I am a woman of sorrowful spirit?
מכאן -- R' Yehoshua ben Levi's own derivation from 'the woman who stood with you here'
'I am the woman who stood with you here' (1 Sam 1:26)
'and Hannah spoke on her heart' -- concerning the matters of her heart
from the day the Holy One created His world no person called the Holy One 'Tzevaot' until Hannah came and called Him Tzevaot -- 'and she vowed a vow and said: Lord of Hosts' (I Sam 1:11)
Hannah before the Holy One: Master of the world, of all the hosts upon hosts You created in Your world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one son?

a parable: like a flesh-and-blood king who made a feast for his servants; a poor man at the door, ignored, pushed in to the king: my lord the king, of the whole feast you made, is it hard in your eyes to give me one slice?
שנאמר ותתפלל על ה׳, מלמד שהטיחה דברים כלפי מעלה
Hannah spoke impertinently toward on High
שנאמר ואתה הסבת את לבם אחרנית
Elijah spoke impertinently toward on High
שנאמר ונקתה ונזרעה זרע -- the acquitted woman conceives, so God would not make His Torah false
Hannah: I will go and seclude myself before Elkana my husband; once I have secluded myself they will give me the sota water, and You will not make Your Torah false

אם כן, ילכו כל העקרות כולן ויסתתרו, וזו שלא קלקלה -- נפקדת! אלא... -- if the verse promised the barren conception, every barren woman would seclude herself; so the verse must promise easier childbirth
R' Yishmael: 'she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed' teaches that if she was barren she is remembered

הניחא למאן דאמר אם היתה עקרה נפקדת שפיר, אלא למאן דאמר אם היתה יולדת בצער יולדת בריוח... מאי איכא למימר? -- Hannah's threat works only if the sota water makes a barren woman conceive; on the reading that it only eases childbirth, what can be said?
מאי אם ראה תראה -- דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם: on that reading the doubled verb is ordinary idiom and yields no threat (= p_dibra_torah_kilshon_bnei_adam, held only aliba R' Akiva)
what is 'if You will look' [for the one who reads Num 5:28 as R' Akiva]? -- the Torah spoke in human idiom
R' Elazar: 'if You will look' -- Hannah said before the Holy One: if You look, well; and if not, You will see

שנאמר וישחטו את הפר ויביאו את הנער אל עלי -- משום דוישחטו את הפר הביאו הנער אל עלי? because they slaughtered the bull they brought the youth to Eli? (the juxtaposition is explained by the story that follows)
Samuel was one who taught halakha in the presence of his teacher
מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה, מכאן לשחיטה שכשרה בזר -- since the priests' mitzva begins at receiving the blood, slaughter is valid by a non-priest
Eli: call a priest -- let him come and slaughter
Eli: and whoever teaches halakha in the presence of his teacher is liable to death
שלש אמתות הללו למה -- the verse's threefold 'Your maidservant' is what he expounds
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: the three 'maidservants' are there because of the three [mitzvot] of death You created in woman
'the affliction of Your maidservant... and not forget Your maidservant... and give Your maidservant' (1 Sam 1:11) -- three times 'Your maidservant'
whoever sits in a fast on Shabbat -- they tear up his decree of seventy years
what is his remedy?
שנאמר משה ואהרן בכהניו ושמואל בקוראי שמו -- R' Yochanan's own derivation from Ps 99:6
Rav: [she asked for] a man among men
'and give Your maidservant seed of men' (1 Sam 1:11)
Rav Dimi: not tall and not short, not small and not fat, not pale and not ruddy, not wise and not foolish
